ground_truth.description: _claimFees() sweeps the entire balance of `token0`/`token1` after `collectFees()`, stealing rewards if `rewardToken` matches `token0` or `token1`. Impact: Bribe contract receives staking rewards instead of fees.
ground_truth.root_cause: _claimFees() sweeps the entire balance of `token0`/`token1` after `collectFees()`, stealing rewards if `rewardToken` matches `token0` or `token1`. Impact: Bribe contract receives staking rewards instead of fees.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: A test deposits 10 HYBR rewards, adds 0.1 HYBR fees, and `claimFees()` sweeps all 10.1 HYBR to the bribe contract.
ground_truth.fix_description: Transfer only the difference in balance before/after `collectFees()`; add access control to `claimFees`. Status: Mitigation confirmed.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The function sweeps the entire token0/token1 balance after collectFees(), which includes any reward tokens if rewardToken matches token0 or token1. This steals staking rewards intended for users.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Reward token is same as token0 (e.g., HYBR). 2. Gauge receives 10 HYBR rewards via notifyRewardAmount(). 3. Pool accumulates 0.1 HYBR fees. 4. Anyone calls claimFees(). 5. Function transfers 10.1 HYBR to bribe contract instead of just 0.1 HYBR fees.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Track balance before/after collectFees(): uint256 balanceBefore0 = IERC20(_token0).balanceOf(address(this)); clPool.collectFees(); claimed0 = IERC20(_token0).balanceOf(address(this)) - balanceBefore0;

prediction.overall_explanation: The contract contains one critical logic error where _claimFees() incorrectly transfers the entire contract balance of token0/token1 instead of only newly collected fees. This allows theft of staking rewards when reward tokens match pool tokens. Other functions appear correctly implemented with reentrancy protection and access controls.
